name: Montana Precision Products
old_description: Montana Precision Products, a joint venture between SeaCast, Inc. and GE Aviation, was founded in 2012 and currently employs about 190 people. MPP specializes in welded tube/duct assemblies and structural castings for aerospace and commercial applications.
about:
Montana Precision Products operates from Butte, Montana, where it was established in 2012 as a joint venture between SeaCast, Inc. and GE Aviation. The partnership combined SeaCast's investment casting expertise with GE Aviation's aerospace engineering resources to serve the commercial and defense aviation markets.

The company produces welded tube and duct assemblies, small structural investment castings, and a newer line of flex joints designed to absorb thermal expansion and vibration in engine and airframe ducting systems. Its 97,000-square-foot facility houses vacuum and air melt furnaces for nickel super alloys, stainless and alloy steels, and cobalt alloys, along with 4-axis CNC machining centers, a horizontal turning center, and a range of welding and tube-forming equipment. About 190 employees work across two shifts, handling everything from melt chemical analysis to final inspection.

MPP's customer base centers on the aerospace sector, supplying net-shape castings and welded assemblies for commercial and military engine programs. The flex joints product line, launched after the 2022 expansion, targets engine and aircraft ducting systems where movement absorption is critical. The company also serves commercial applications that require high-integrity metal components.

Leadership emphasizes a mission built on teamwork, technical innovation, and continual improvement to deliver world-class net-shape castings and welded assemblies. The 2022 expansion added 56,000 square feet specifically to launch the flex joints line, which the board chairman described as a significant engineering and operational achievement that strengthens MPP's role in the international aerospace supply chain.
